name: Service Revolver
desc: Six chambers. The serial number has been filed off by someone — possibly you.

name: Medical Bag
desc: Scalpels, sutures, morphine ampoules, and a stethoscope that sometimes hears two hearts.

name: Field Dressing Kit
desc: Bandages, iodine, and a steady quantity of practical experience.

name: Toolbox
desc: Wrenches, pliers, wire, and a hammer that has settled arguments.

name: Prayer Book
desc: Worn smooth at the psalms for the dying. Some pages are underlined in a hand you don't recognize.

name: Annotated Monograph
desc: Your own published work, margins black with corrections in your handwriting — dated next year.

name: Press Notebook
desc: Shorthand nobody else can read. The last page already has tomorrow's headline.

name: Violin in a Battered Case
desc: It stays in tune no matter what. Lately that has begun to feel sinister.

name: Set of Lockpicks
desc: Rolled in oilcloth. Illegal in four countries, indispensable in this one.

name: Planchette
desc: The board burned years ago. The pointer survived, and still moves at night.

name: Railway Carriage Key
desc: A standard-issue square-shank carriage key. It fits this train's locks. It should not.

name: Engraved Calling Cards
desc: Cream stock, fine engraving. The name printed on them is almost yours.

name: Iron Spanner
desc: Heavy, honest, and indifferent to what it hits.

name: Hunting Knife
desc: Skinned everything the north woods offered. Keeps its edge.

name: Locked Briefcase
desc: You have carried it for years. You have never had the key.

name: Undertaker's Measuring Cord
desc: Knotted at intervals for measuring the deceased. Lately it measures people on its own.

name: Kitchen Knife
desc: Balanced for boning. Perfectly ordinary, which is worth a great deal here.

name: Brass Hand Bell
desc: Rings clear over any noise. On this train, things listen when it rings.

name: Bindle and Bedroll
desc: Everything needed to sleep anywhere, and to leave without a trace.

name: Wedding Ring
desc: Warm even in the cold. The inscription inside has one letter too many.

name: Family Photograph
desc: Faces you love. One of them is slightly turned away in every copy you've ever owned.

name: Pocket Watch
desc: Keeps perfect time. Aboard this train, that makes it the only one of its kind.

name: Bloodstained Letter
desc: You know it by weight. You have never once dared to reread it.

name: Child's Wooden Horse
desc: Paint worn away where a small hand held it. You cannot remember whose.

name: Dented Hip Flask
desc: Whatever you pour in, it is always half full. Never more.

name: Unmarked Train Ticket
desc: Destination: TERMINUS. No date, no seat, no price. It has never been punched.

name: Traveler's Medal
desc: A saint's medal for protection on journeys. The saint's face has been worn entirely away.

name: Storm Lantern
desc: Burns lantern oil. The circle of light it casts is the truest place on the train.

name: Surgical Scalpel
desc: It was something else in another carriage. Here, it is exactly what the doctors use.

name: Small Compartment Key
desc: It was a toy a moment ago. Now it is brass, numbered 7, and cold.

name: Ticket Punched in Blood
desc: The punch-hole is a neat dark oval. Locked doors treat it as authority.

name: Officially Punched Ticket
desc: Clipped by the Conductor's own punch. Valid, the way a verdict is valid.

name: Bundle of Undelivered Letters
desc: Every envelope is addressed to someone aboard. Some are addressed to you.

name: Vial of Hospital Sedative
desc: The label lists a dosage for 'passengers of unusual condition.'

name: Votive Candle from the Chapel
desc: It burns with a steady flame that leans toward the engine, always.

name: Shard of Mirror-Glass
desc: Reflections in it lag half a second behind. Useful, if you can bear to look.

name: The Conductor's Ticket Punch
desc: Heavy nickel. The jaws are stained. It punches more than paper.

name: Guard's Signal Lamp
desc: Shows red or white. Train servants obey its signals without thinking.

name: Sodden Operating Manual
desc: Half the pages describe machinery. The other half describe feeding.
